home.heroDesc: Pit yourself against GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Muse Spark, Mistral, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, GLM, or MiniMax across five classic boards.
home.rules1: Human vs model, or model vs model — with spectating and auto-play built in.
home.rules2: The model chooses each move entirely on its own.
home.rules3: The app parses the move and decides the result by the game rules.
home.rules4: Three illegal model outputs in one match also count as a loss.
home.rules5: If you leave the play page, the match ends with no winner.
home.aboutDesc: This project is a fun experiment that tests each model's own board-game strength — how smart it really is. Difficulty is adjustable, so it's also nice for beginners and kids learning board games against models. The project is open source — explore the <source>source code</source>.

games.gomokuDesc: 15×15 free-style, five in a row wins.
games.goDesc: Captures and simple ko; ends after two passes.
games.othelloDesc: 8×8 Reversi. Flip discs; most discs wins.

arena.title: Arena
arena.subtitle: Choose a game and matchup mode, then configure the model.
arena.reasoningHint: Maps to each provider’s reasoning / thinking knobs. Higher levels are slower and use more tokens, but smarter.
arena.reasoningOffHint: Turns off the model’s reasoning / thinking. Higher levels are slower and use more tokens, but smarter.
arena.reasoningOffModelInvalid: Reasoning Off requires a model that can disable thinking. Pick another model or raise Reasoning.
arena.legalMovesProtectionHint: Reminds the model to reduce illegal moves in Chess, Othello, and Xiangqi. Turn it off to better test the model's own ability.
arena.legalMovesProtectionNA: Not available for this game — Go and Gomoku do not send a legal-move list.
arena.tacticalGuidanceHint: Reminds the model to play actively when safe and avoid giving pieces away. Turn it off to better test the model's own ability.
arena.missingKey: Missing API key for {provider}. Configure it in <keys>Keys</keys>.
arena.sameModelBothSides: White and Black must use different models.

stats.title: Match statistics
stats.thinkDesc: Average time from starting an LLM request to accepting a legal move, split by reasoning level.
stats.failuresDesc: Persisted failed attempts from move history. Illegal columns are counted strikes, split by reasoning level. Soft failures (refusals, safety / content filters, etc.) do not count as strikes.
stats.abortedHint: Matches that ended with no winner — left the play page, manually ended, or (MvM) still rate-limited after two retries.
stats.playerRecordDesc: By the name you entered. Players without a name are counted in one Human row.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: Welcome to chess5.ai (“the Service”). By using the Service, you agree to these Terms of Service, which also cover how we handle data (privacy). If you do not agree, please do not use the Service.
terms.s1Body: chess5.ai is an experimental, open-source project for Human vs LLM and Model vs Model play across Chess, Go, Xiangqi, Gomoku, and Othello. The Service may change, break, or stop without notice. It is provided as-is for experimentation and learning.
terms.s2Body: You bring your own API keys for third-party model providers. Keys stay in your browser (encrypted local storage) and are not persisted to our server database or disk; each model call is forwarded only through our temporary proxy. You are responsible for keeping those keys safe, for any usage charges from those providers, and for complying with each provider’s terms. Do not share keys you are not allowed to use.
terms.s3Body: We do not require user accounts. API keys are encrypted in your browser’s local storage and are sent to model providers only through our temporary proxy; they are not written to a server-side database or file, and we do not keep a lasting copy after the proxy request finishes. Because the decryption key is stored in the same browser, this encryption guards against casual inspection rather than malicious scripts or browser extensions. Match-related data (such as game type, mode, moves, results, optional player display names, and short-lived presence heartbeats) may be stored on the server to run matches and show statistics. Rate limiting may use short-lived request metadata such as IP address. When you use a provider with your key, that provider’s own privacy policy also applies to the request content you send.
terms.s4Body: Do not abuse, attack, or overload the Service; do not attempt to bypass security or access other users’ matches without authorization; and do not use the Service for unlawful purposes. We may refuse or interrupt access if misuse harms the Service or others.
terms.s5Body: Models choose moves on their own; the app validates moves and decides outcomes by game rules. Too many illegal model outputs in one match can count as a loss. Leaving the play page may end a match with no winner. Optional Arena settings (such as reasoning, legal-move protection, and tactical guidance) change difficulty and prompt content; turning them off is closer to testing a model’s raw ability.
terms.s6Body: Families may use the Service to play and learn board games together. If a child uses the Service, a parent or guardian should supervise, manage any API keys, and decide what settings are appropriate. Do not submit personal information about children beyond an optional short display name.
terms.s7Body: Model moves, comments, and results are not guaranteed to be correct, fair, or suitable for any purpose. The Service is not professional advice. To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for losses from key misuse, provider bills, downtime, data loss, or reliance on model output.
terms.s8Body: The project source code is available on GitHub. Using the code is subject to the repository’s license; these Terms govern use of the hosted Service.
terms.s9Body: Questions about these Terms: reach out via X (@wilsonye2025) or the GitHub repository for chess5.
terms.s10Body: We may update these Terms from time to time. Continued use of the Service after changes means you accept the updated Terms. The “Last updated” date at the top will change when we revise this page.
